{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABikTCzQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhL7Qp4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 239, "title": "Expose HDD Save directly and separate disk replacement from secondary actions", "body": "## Problem

Issue #237 / PR #238 implemented safe manual HDD persistence and automatic restoration at startup. However, the user must open the IDE HDD **Change…** picker to find **Save disk**. Saving is not changing the disk; the primary action is hidden under an unrelated label. Since saving is manual, this is particularly easy to overlook.

The maintainer approved the following HDD-only UI concept: a visible Save button, a separate Change button, an overflow menu for less frequent operations, and a small save-status line.

## Expected UI

Illustrative wireframe (adapt to the existing sidebar width and typography):

```
IDE HDD
Game-Install.hdi
[ Save ] [ Change… ] [ ⋮ ]
Unsaved changes
```

- **Save**: visible directly in the mounted IDE HDD section, not inside a popover. Use the existing green accent for a clear primary action, particularly when changes are unsaved. One click starts the current save operation; no file chooser or unnecessary confirmation.
- **Change…**: changes the mounted HDD, using the current local-file selection/import workflow and its data-loss safeguards. When empty, use Insert… instead.
- **Overflow (⋮)**: a compact, accessible menu for existing Export disk, Eject, and Restore previous checkpoint actions as applicable. Do not duplicate Save under Change or the overflow menu.
- **Status**: a small, always discoverable line in the HDD slot indicating relevant states such as Not saved, Unsaved changes, Saving…, Saved, or a recoverable save error. A saved timestamp is optional if it fits naturally. An imported disk that has never been saved must not be labeled Saved just because no guest writes have occurred. Do not falsely indicate durable success before the checkpoint commits.
- Keep the existing light neutral style, restrained green accents, typography and compact spacing from #233. Do not redesign the emulator screen, CRT bezel, header, toolbar, machine selector or floppy slots. The approved mockup is an illustration of the HDD controls, not a request to restyle the entire application.

## Implementation notes

- Inspect [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) (`#slot-2`, `#drive-2`, `#media-picker`, `#save-hdd`, `#recover-hdd`), [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) (picker state, save handler, `mounted[2].checkpoint`, `savedWrites`, `hdi_write_count`, busy/error handling), and [web/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/style.css).
- Reuse the existing save action and transaction/storage implementation from #237/#238. Moving the button must not introduce another persistence path. Bind its action explicitly to the HDD rather than depending on which floppy picker was last opened.
- Move the existing HDD status out of the picker. Use existing checkpoint and write-count information, with lightweight bounded refresh if needed. Do not scan, hash or copy the disk just to refresh the status; avoid high-frequency RPC or per-frame polling. Preserve gameplay/audio performance. Keep manual saving; automatic saving is out of scope.
- Reflect existing availability and busy state: no save when no HDD is mounted, a save is already running, or the operation is unsupported in the current machine state. Keep the status truthful after import, save, recovery, replacement, eject, profile switch, and failed/canceled operations. Permit retry and export after recoverable failures.
- Preserve current OPFS/IndexedDB checkpoint safety, Web Locks, previous-generation recovery, automatic startup restoration, Save/Export distinction, unsaved-write confirmations, and pause/resume behavior. Do not change their implementation merely for UI polish.
- Keep the three actions compact and accessible in the existing responsive HDD slot. Provide an accessible name for the overflow button (e.g. HDD actions), keyboard operation, Escape dismissal and sensible focus return. Long filenames/status text must not resize the emulator screen or cause horizontal overflow.
- Update current Help and README instructions to say that Save is directly in the HDD section and describe the new overflow location.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance (bounded)

1. A mounted HDD exposes a directly visible Save button independent of Change; Save works without first opening a picker. Verify an actual guest disk change, save, reload, and automatic restoration with existing persistence tests adapted to the new user flow.
2. Change only selects/replaces media; the HDD overflow exposes Export, Eject and Restore previous checkpoint as appropriate. Existing confirmations, cancellation, recovery and floppy actions remain functional.
3. The status correctly distinguishes a never-saved or modified disk, saving, committed save and failure in ordinary use. No misleading Saved state after a failed save.
4. The HDD controls fit representative desktop and narrow/mobile layouts, are keyboard accessible, and preserve the screen-first layout. Provide a small screenshot or equivalent visual evidence using FreeDOS or an original test fixture.
5. Run relevant existing browser/storage checks and required CI. Reuse the existing persistence implementation and validation where unchanged; do not expand into a new persistence design, exhaustive race-case investigation or unrelated UI work.

This is a narrowly scoped HDD action-layout improvement. Once the above works and mandatory checks pass, merge without requiring additional visual polish or unrelated changes.

Related: #237 / #238 (HDD persistence), #233 (player layout).
